question: Totaram Sharma, Pandit Ayodhya Prasad, Gopal Das and Babu Ram Shanker Pagaldas are noted players of which of the following instruments?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pakhawaj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• **Pakhawaj** is a barrel-shaped drum traditionally used in Hindustani classical music.

• The instrument is similar to the **mridangam**, which is used in Carnatic classical music.

• It is played horizontally and usually accompanies the **dhrupad** style of singing.

• The Pakhawaj is known for its deep, resonant sound and is made of wood with a leather drumhead on each end.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Sarod**

• The Sarod is a stringed instrument used mainly in Indian classical music.

• It is known for its deep, weighty, introspective sound and is an important concert instrument in Hindustani music.

• The Sarod is played with a plectrum made of coconut shell, and the strings are pressed with the fingernails to produce a clear sound.

• **Mridangam**

• The Mridangam is a percussion instrument originating from South India.

• It is the primary rhythmic accompaniment in a Carnatic music ensemble.

• The Mridangam is an ancient instrument and is considered the precursor to the Pakhawaj.

• **Sarangi**

• The Sarangi is a bowed, short-necked string instrument from India.

• It is an important instrument in Hindustani classical music and is known for its ability to mimic the human voice.

• The Sarangi has three main playing strings and a number of sympathetic strings that resonate along with the played notes.
